title: ITX 3-18: Expeditionary Fire Rescue
description: U.S. Marines with Marine Wing Support Squadron 271 conduct an expeditionary fire rescue exercise during Integrated Training Exercise (ITX) 3-18 aboard Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center, Twentynine Palms, Calif., April 30, 2018. ITX is a large-scale, combined-arms training exercise intended to produce combat-ready forces capable of operating as an integrated Marine air-ground task force. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Paige Stade)
keywords: MWSS-271, 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing, ITX. ITX 3-18

transcript.text: (sirens wailing)
^- Today we did a evaled simulated,
^on a CH-53 hard landing with three souls on board,
and second fire present. (sirens wailing)
Three souls means there's three either downed pilots,
three chiefs, or anybody that was aboard the aircraft.
We had really good communication.
We worked well as a team.
Everyone knew what they were supposed to be doing.
There were some curve balls that were thrown.
We had some malfunctions with our gear
that could have been alleviated in the beginning,
but there's always improvements that could be had.
(hoses spraying)
We train everyday out here, at least we try to.
We have been doing pieces at a time,
you know, crawl, walk, run,
and we're not necessarily at the run phase yet out here.
There's birds that we haven't seen,
or aircraft that we have not seen
back in our home unit in Bogue Airfield,
but we're always ready for an emergency
if something happens.
